faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.

faqs.question: A label peeled off in the product. How should I remove it?
faqs.answer:
Press the product's
LF/FF
button until the label appears on the platen and remove the label. If you can't remove the label this way, do not remove the platen from the product. Get the printer serviced.
Note:
We recommend you use the pull tractor to print labels. Labels fed through the rear push tractor can curl and peel off under the platen.

faqs.question: What is the recommended duty cycle for my product?
faqs.answer: The recommended duty cycle is 25%. Epson America's definition of a 25% duty cycle is the printer printing (not idle) for two hours per day (25% of an eight hour day) for 22 days per month.

faqs.question: When I print a multiple page document on single sheets, the first page prints correctly but the pages after that start printing too low. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
The difference in print position is usually caused by the page length setting in your software. Most programs have a default page length of 66 lines per page when using 11” continuous paper.
When you use single sheets, however, the printer automatically provides a small top and bottom margin. Since the top and bottom margins are non-printable areas, the maximum number of lines per page is reduced from 66 to 61 lines per page.
Many programs have an option to change the number of lines per page. You should change the number of lines per page to 61. If your software offers a selection for “cut-sheet feeder” or “single sheet” (or a similar wording), select that paper type in the software settings.

faqs.question: How do I create a custom paper size in the Server Properties?
faqs.answer:
Follow these steps to create a new page size accessible by all printer drivers installed in Windows:
Open the
Printers
or
Printers and Faxes
window.
Click
File
, then
Server Properties
.
Put a check in the
Create a new form
box.
Input a name for the custom paper size.
Under
Paper Size
, enter the desired height and width.
Click
Save
or
Save Form
to add the new form size to the list, then
OK
to close Server Properties.

faqs.question: I'm printing serial, my baud rate is at 9600, and intermittently my product will lose data. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
If you are using the non-buffered serial interface card (model C823051) and X-on/X-off is enabled, the X-off signal may not reach the printer in time to delay data transmission. This will result in an overflow and loss of data.
If you can use a DTR setting, change X-on/X-off to DTR. If you must use X-on/X-off, try decreasing the baud rate. See
Setting the conditions
for the model C823051 Serial Interface Card.
Another option would be to purchase a 32KB buffered serial interface card (model C823071). The buffered card has a flag reset timing feature which allows the card to set aside additional buffer space to "catch" any data overflow. The flag reset timing feature settings are selectable through dip switches on the card.
Also, make sure your printer cable is less than 50 feet long when you're printing at 9600 baud.

faqs.question: Why does my product stop or pause in the middle of a print job?
faqs.answer:
The printer has a built-in sensor that monitors the temperature of the print head. When the print head begins to get too hot, it may pause or slow down to prevent overheating. If the print head begins to overheat, thermistor will stop the print head completely until it has cooled down. Once the print head has sufficiently cooled down, the printer will resume the print job.
The printer may also stop or pause because it is waiting for more data or because it is processing data already received.

faqs.question: Does the product have dip switches to set up my product configuration?
faqs.answer:
The LQ-590 has no DIP switches. You can
change the printer's default settings
using the printer's control panel default-setting mode or the Epson Remote Configuration Manager.

faqs.question: Can I use the knob on the side of my product to load and/or adjust paper?
faqs.answer:
No, never use the knob to load or adjust the paper. The knob should only be used to clear paper jams after the printer has been turned off.
Use the Micro Adjust function
to adjust the paper.

faqs.question: Why won't my product print serially from my computer?
faqs.answer:
There are a few possibilities:
Make sure your optional Epson serial interface card is set up properly.
See
Setting the conditions
for the model C823051 Serial Interface Card
See
Setting the conditions
for the model C823071 Serial Interface Card
If you are using a straight through modem cable, change the cable to a null modem cable.
If you are already using a null modem cable, ensure that the settings for the printer's serial port match the settings on your computer.
There is always the possibility of a loose connection or a bad cable. Disconnect and reconnect the cable on the PC and the printer and try printing again. If you are still experiencing problems, try a different cable.
The problem may be related to your computer's serial port. Try using the printer on another computer to determine whether that is the case.

faqs.question: Can I connect my product to IBM mainframe (IBM 3270) and IBM minicomputer (AS/400 or System 3X) environments?
faqs.answer:
Yes.
For IBM mainframe environments, you can purchase an optional Type-B Coax interface card (model C823141) which allows direct connectivity and emulates the following IBM printer models: 3287, 3268, 4214-1, and 4224 (non IPDS).
For IBM minicomputer environments, you can purchase an optional Type-B Twinax interface card (model C823151) which allows direct connectivity and emulates the following IBM printer models: 4210, 4214, 5225, 5224, 5256, 5219, and 3812.

faqs.question: Does my product support IBM emulation?
faqs.answer: The printer supports IBM 2390 Plus mode emulation.
